name: nlp_rag_index_bad
title: A RAG index built through a training-mode encoder, whitened with a PCA fitted on the dev queries and refitted again at evaluation time
origin: hardening round 2, domain-nlp, 2026-09-14 - the defective twin of nlp_rag_index
note: Six planted defects, four of which a rule models, two found today. The two misses are measured holes: MLV301/MLV302 cannot see a batched-inference loop that iterates range(0, len(texts), batch_size) instead of a DataLoader, and nothing declares that blindness (NLP2-05); MLV102 declares its own silence through an untagged_dataflow diagnostic because the vectors are numpy arrays produced by a workspace function, which is the honest behaviour.

expected.symbol: for start in range(0, len(texts), batch_size)
expected.defect: the encoder is never put in eval mode - the correct twin's model.eval() calls have been deleted from both callers
expected.why: PooledEncoder carries nn.Dropout(0.1), so every vector written into the index is produced through a randomly thinned network and two identical passages get different embeddings

expected.symbol: for start in range(0, len(texts), batch_size)
expected.defect: encode_texts has lost the @torch.no_grad() decorator; only a trailing .detach() keeps the result usable
expected.why: the whole corpus is encoded with the autograd graph live, which is the classic indexing out-of-memory

expected.defect: the PCA whitener is fitted on np.vstack([corpus_vectors, query_vectors]) - the dev queries are part of the fit
expected.why: the embedding space is rotated to suit the evaluation queries, so recall@10 measured on them is optimistic and does not transfer

expected.defect: the whitener is refitted on the dev query vectors at evaluation time, so it no longer matches the transform the index was built with
expected.why: corpus vectors and query vectors end up in two different spaces: the inner products are meaningless and the metric is silently wrong rather than an error

expected.defect: the device is hard-coded to cuda with no availability check
expected.why: the index build cannot run on the CPU box that holds the corpus

expected.defect: the same hard-coded device in the evaluation entrypoint
the correct twin's torch.manual_seed / np.random.seed pair has been deleted
expected.why: with dropout live during indexing (see MLV301) the index itself is different on every build, so recall@10 is not reproducible

forbidden.why: there is no train/test split call anywhere in this project - the defect is a fit on the evaluation queries, which is MLV102's, not a fit before a split
no DataLoader is constructed anywhere in this project
the same - there is no DataLoader here
the same, and both entrypoints sit behind an if __name__ == "__main__" guard
there is no training loop in this project - nothing calls backward()
encode_texts accumulates CPU tensors, and the .detach() on line 48 is what keeps them out of the graph
recall@k and MRR@k are rank metrics over parent ids, not a classifier score
no CrossEntropyLoss exists in this project
no sigmoid and no BCE loss appear in this project
tokenize() moves every tensor to the device before the forward (line 40)
both submodules are assigned directly to attributes (lines 23-24)
the index is written with faiss.write_index (line 65); torch.save and torch.load do not appear

unsupported.defect: IndexFlatIP is an inner-product index but the whitened vectors are no longer unit norm, so the search returns dot products rather than cosine similarities
unsupported.why: MLView has no knowledge table for faiss at all - it says so in an unresolved_callee diagnostic - and no rule relates a normalisation to an index metric

unsupported.symbol: encode_texts(model, tokenizer, [q["question"] for q in queries], device)
unsupported.defect: evaluate() rebuilds the whole index through build() on every call, so the corpus is re-encoded for every metric run
the transform applied at query time is not the transform applied at index time - a train/serve skew inside one program
unsupported.why: MLV901 (preprocessing applied in training but missing on the inference path) is a later-tier rule and is not built; MLV102 covers the fit-on-test half of the same line
